UNIVERSITY 


Mt ‘al Leadership Devel t Fund 


We lost a community leader; educational innovator; 
consummate teacher and mentor with the passing of A. Ross 
Seaman on October 23, 1987. His death is a loss to countless people 
from the many places where he expended his energies and warmth to 
help others become the best they could be. Those who knew Ross best 
remember him for being on the leading edge of bringing the best 
possible resources to bear on the issues that engaged his energy; 
camping and leadership training, recreation leadership and 

; community organization, particularly when it related 
to adolescent lire, and latterly, when it related to an 
aging population. One colleague referred to him as a 
cheerleader for the human race and this special 
quality which he possessed and shared so generously, 
warrants remembrance on our part. 


One of Ross’s philosophies was to “pass it on” 

whenever he was on the receiving end of something 
meaningful and important to him. The A. Ross Seaman Leadership 
Development Fund will enable students in a variety of leadership 
areas to pursue studies and/or experiences that will further their 
own leadership potential and skills. In this way Ross will remain 
with us, and his impact on our own growth and development will 
continue to be felt by those who follow in his footsteps.

lenge 15-year-old campers in the areas of teamwork and cooperation, canoe trip- 
ping, outdoor leadership, naturalism, and personal growth. 


Héléna's work on the Rangers program will help to ensure Kanawana's role in 
developing leadership for years to come. I'm sure A. Ross Seaman would have 
been proud to call her a Kanawanian!

"Abed Lriste " 


1988 - The first cup was held in the spring of 1988 at the Loyola Campus of Concordia University. The 
competition was between the students of the Leisure Studies Program at Concordia and the students from the 
Community Recreation Leadership Training program at Dawson College. The activity for this event was touch 
football, played on a very snowy field. Following the touch football game, the participants gathered at the Golden 
Moon Restaurant for supper. The evening program held at the Loyola Campus Center included a guest lecturer. 


1989 - The Dawson College students organized the second cup. It was held at Westmount High School. The 
activity for the day was volleyball. Following the activity participants were treated to a supper prepared by the 
students of Dawson College. The guest speakers for the evening were Gavin Turley of the YMCA and Don Lee of 
Executive Registry. Donations totalling $85 were collected. 


1990 - The cup this year was held at the Loyola arena. The activity was broomball. Students dressed in a variety 
of hats and a carnival atmosphere was created. The evening activity was skits, discussions & a cheer from each 
group. A cheque of $700.00 was presented to the A. Ross Seaman Committee. 


1991 - This year the cup was held at the Beaconsfield Recreation Center. The CRLT students organized floor 
hockey and Kamp Kanawana made their debut. The evening activity included a buffet supper and students 
talking about leadership. An auction, which included many items of memorabilia from Ross’ past, raised $765.65. 


1992 - The Leisure Studies Class under the supervision of Dick Cuttell organized the cup for this year at the 
Concordia Sports Complex. Space ball was the activity followed by a buffet supper served in the lobby. An auction 
at the Loyola Campus Center and Leadership theme skits prepared by Dawson College students, Leisure Studies 
students and Kamp Kanawana councillors rounded out the day. 


1993 - The same Leisure Studies class once again organized this year's program. It was held at the Loyola 
gymnasium and the guest speakers were Laurence Lang and Randy Swedburg. The activity was "Kinball", with 
each organization providing crazy relay games. Following the activity a supper supplied by all organizations was 
held in the basement of St. Ignatius Church. This year the auction raised approximately $2,800. 


1994 - The program continued to be organized by the class from the Leisure Studies. Activities included a Murder 
mystery game and co-operative type games run by each organization. For the first time children from the YMCA 
were present - an after school program. The evening activities were held at Monkland Tennis Club where supper 
took on a tropical flavour. An invited speaker, Kirk Fontaine, addressed the gathering and the traditional auction 
raised approximately $2,200. 


1995 - Dawson College students created a committee with the YMCA, Kamp Kanawana and Concordia students 
to organize this year's program. The afternoon activities were held at the Westmount YMCA where we were able 
to purchase home baked goodies. Following an afternoon of co-operative barnyard games including, line dancing, 
and a supper was held at the Dawson College Atwater campus. Country fair type games and "How well did you 
know Ross" were played following the supper and this year the auction raised $ 1,200.00. 


1996 - This year's program was organized by a group of students from Leisure Studies as part of their course. 
Also involved were students from CRLT. The event was held at Dawson College, where for the first time, the 
recipients of the scholarship were presented their awards together and past recipients attending were also 
acknowledged. A booklet was prepared identifying all the recipients and the reason they won the award. The 
guest speaker was Charlie Poxon of the M.D.C. Police, a former student of Ross’ at CRLT. A buffet supper, 
supplied by the students, was served. Afterwards, carnival type games were held and those lucky enough won 
tickets enabling them to win door prizes! 


(A brief history ...cont'd.) 


1997 - The 10th Anniversary celebration was held at Dawson College Campus. Former A. Ross Seaman Award 
recipients, C.R.L.T. and RALSA representatives, were this year's organizers. Renowned author Stuart MacLean, 
broadcaster and professor of Journalism at Ryerson Poly technical Institute, recollected antidotes from Ross' 
friends. Awards were given to the 1996 recipients, followed by a buffet supper and an auction. Prior to the event 
students were given the chance to "earn" A.R.S. fun money by fund raising, volunteering for the event, and 
answering questions in class; which enabled them to bid on items during the "student-only” auction. Over $990 
was raised this year. Mystery clues were available through newsletters and the night of the event to discover 
"Who is Rae Creation?" The answer: EVERYONE! 


1998 - As this was the last year, before the merger, they would be known as the Applied Social Science Student 
Association, the committee decided to host the event. The event was held at Dawson College where a mixer, 
planned by CRLT, was played before the awards. The guest speaker was Paul Cappelli, a long time friend and 
colleague of Ross'. Following a supper donated by students, faculty and others an auction was held raising over 
$1900. The evening ended with students from the various agencies entertaining us in many ways. 


1999 - Our event was once again held at Dawson College, which has proven to be an excellent location over the 
years. Our guest speaker, Mike Lieberman, shared with us his memories of Ross. The YMCA of Montreal, YMCA 
Kamp Kanawana and Dawson College CRLT provided food and beverages to sustain our participants during the 
evening. The auction raised $1,016.00 for the fund following the presentation of awards. The use of our special 
guests as auctioneers proved to be very entertaining. After a long evening, participants went home well fed and 
having done a good deed in participating in Ross' legacy. 


2000 - The new millennium marked a new twist in the Awards Event. For the first time, the traditional auction 
changed to an extensive silent auction format, which met with great reviews and successful revenues that were 
put back into the fund. The highlight of the evening was the guest speaker Bonnie Miller, a former graduate from 
C.R.L.T. Bonnie gave a realistic and touching picture into her experience as a student with Ross and all had great 
fun. Ross' name was carried on for yet another year! 


2001 - We survived a snowstorm this year, and despite the unfortunate weather, we had one of our best turnouts, 
which speak volumes for Ross and his memory. To help guests reflect and experience who Ross Seaman was, Bill 
Russell gave a touching account of the impact he had on so many organizations and the legacy he has left in his 
place. There were mixer games, food, drink, merriment, and auction that spanned the evening raising over 
$1400.00. The theme reflected a tribute to long-time friend of Ross, Dick MacDonald, and scholarship recipients 
from each organization were honoured and will carry his name into the future. 


2002 - Mr. Gavin Turley set the tone at this year's A. Ross Seaman event, recounting many memorable 
experiences he had with Ross. It was a great turnout yet again by the organizations involved and the silent 
auction created the most suspense, as the bidding wars with A. Ross Seaman fun money escalated. The recipients 
represented themselves well and reminded all of us that leadership defines our character as well as our 


profession. 


2008 - Johanne Cyr, Dawson College Graduate and one of Ross' students, began the award ceremonies with 
heartfelt memories of Ross and his dedication to the continuous growth and development of his students. This 
year's scholarship recipients shared many of the leadership qualities for which Ross exemplified. The evening was 
a great success with over 100 guests, friends, and family members joining-in the festivities. It was wonderful to 
see so many familiar faces, notably Concordia and Dawson CRLT alumni. Once again, this year's big winners in 
the silent auction for the Kamp Kanawana weekend were the students from Dawson CRLT.

In 2004 and subsequent years, awards presentations are decentralized at a time and 
place best suited for their individual community. Special 25th year combined 
celebrations will occur in 2012. This change in policy is ensuring continued success 
meeting the Fund's objectives.
